terms.definition: The wide, short final tube of the digestive tract.
terms.function: Absorbs water and salts and packs waste.
terms.whereItIs: After the small intestine, ending at the rectum.
terms.whyItMatters: It saves water and removes the body's waste.

terms.definition: The main wide tube of the large intestine.
terms.function: Absorbs water and moves waste along.
terms.whereItIs: Making up most of the large intestine.
terms.whyItMatters: It is where most water recovery happens.

terms.definition: The last part of the large intestine that stores waste.
terms.function: Holds solid waste until it leaves the body.
terms.whereItIs: The end of the large intestine.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the body release waste on its own timing.

terms.definition: The helpful bacteria living in the gut, especially the large intestine.
terms.function: Help digest leftover material and make vitamins.
terms.whyItMatters: They are important partners in digestion and health.
